title: How far does the car go on one litre?
description: A car covers two hundred and thirty four point four five kilometres on twelve point six litres of petrol. Both numbers are multiplied by ten so that the divisor is a counting number, the division is done place by place, and the answer is rounded to two decimal places.
teaching_notes: One idea: distance per litre is the distance divided by the litres, and a decimal divisor is made a counting number by multiplying both numbers by ten. Watch for children who stop dividing when the ones run out, or who forget to round.

source: A car covers 234.45 km using 12.6 litres of petrol. What is the distance travelled per litre?
video_script.why: The child has learnt to multiply both numbers by ten before dividing by a decimal, and now uses it to find the distance a car travels on one litre of petrol.
video_script.substitution: the book's own car that covers two hundred and thirty four point four five kilometres on twelve point six litres of petrol
video_script.anchor: A car covers two hundred and thirty four point four five kilometres on twelve point six litres of petrol
video_script.payoff_line: The distance per litre is now known.

final_answer.spoken: about eighteen point six one kilometres per litre

maths_rules: size check: 12.6 × 10 = 126 and 12.6 × 20 = 252, and 234.45 lies between them, so the answer lies between 10 and 20
76 Ones = 760 Tenths, and 760 + 5 = 765 Tenths; 126 × 6 = 756, so 6 Tenths, and 9 Tenths remain
9 Tenths = 90 Hundredths; 126 does not go into 90, so 0 Hundredths; 90 Hundredths = 900 Thousandths; 126 × 7 = 882, so 7 Thousandths, and 18 remain
the quotient is 18.607 and the digits go on; to two decimal places the Thousandths digit 7 is 5 or more, so the answer is about 18.61
video_script.design: One idea: distance per litre is the distance divided by the litres, and the decimal divisor is made a counting number by multiplying both numbers by ten. Assumes the book's example of dividing by a decimal. The quotient is built digit by digit as Ones, Tenths, Hundredths and Thousandths and written as a decimal only on the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, change the nine tenths into ninety hundredths.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One hundred and twenty six does not go into ninety, so the hundredths digit is zero.

<bookmark mark='m4'/>The digits do not stop, so we round to two decimal places. Seven is five or more, so the hundredths digit zero becomes one.
